The guard is doing its documented job; the gap is that NO guard owns single-row loss. (2) DO NOT fix this by telling agents to re-read before writing. Every agent already believes it does; the losing write here came from a flow that produced a full-document baseline, and prose cannot make a stale in-memory snapshot fresh. The CAS/rename path in orch-apply.sh is the place where a stale baseline is mechanically detectable. (3) DO NOT assume the CAS guard already covers it — it demonstrably did not on this occurrence; establish WHY before designing (candidate built from a pre-read snapshot, a bypass env var, or a write that never went through orch-apply.sh at all are all live hypotheses and they have different fixes). (4) DO NOT scope this to the signal drain flow alone until the actor is identified. PO did not observe the write and names no culprit flow; 3e257beba is the commit that PUBLISHED the 131-row state, which is not the same claim as it having authored the loss.

done_tasks.root_cause: MECHANISM (PO-verified by execution 2026-07-29T10:20-10:28Z; supersedes DIAGNOSE-RAG-SERVICE-RESTART-LOOP). TWO STACKED CAUSES. (1) FIXED BASELINE EATS THE CAP: embedder.py _model is a lazy singleton (:37 init None, :51 _ensure_model_loaded) with NO release path — grep of apps/rag-service/**/*.py for unload|.release(|del self._model|gc.collect|empty_cache returns ONLY the :37 initializer, so once loaded the model is resident for the container's life. MEASURED on the live container: cold RSS 50.7 MiB (6.6% of 768 MiB); model load logged 10:24:28.5Z->10:24:48.9Z on the FIRST embed; docker stats immediately after, having served exactly ONE POST /index: 749.9 MiB / 768 MiB = 97.65%. HEADROOM 18.1 MiB. (The embedder docstring's '~600-700 MiB warm' understates live by ~50-150 MiB.) Cap was halved in 2dc1d8c4e (Wed Jun 10 2026, 'reduce memory limits to 512m/768m', diff -memory:1.5g/+memory:768m; rag block docker-compose.yml L165-171) for host-budget reasons and never re-validated against the model's fixed cost. (2) COMPACTION FAILURE-PATH DOES NOT RESET ITS COUNTER — this is a real code defect, NOT tuning. repositories.py compact() :237-259 puts 'self._insert_count = 0' at :251 INSIDE the try, AFTER 'await table.optimize(cleanup_older_than=...)' at :250; the except at :257-259 logs a WARNING and returns NORMALLY without resetting. insert() :230-235 wraps 'await self.compact()' in its own try/except whose handler DOES reset (:235 'self._insert_count = 0  # reset to avoid tight retry loop') — but that handler is UNREACHABLE because compact() already swallowed the exception. NET: on ANY compaction failure the counter stays >= _COMPACT_EVERY, so EVERY SUBSEQUENT INSERT re-fires a full-table optimize() until one attempt happens to win. The code's own comment names the exact failure it fails to prevent. LIVE PROOF of the burst: 2026-07-29T09:02:36.139Z / 09:02:36.140Z / 09:02:40.06Z / 09:02:43.13Z all 'compaction failed (non-fatal)' -> 09:02:44.17Z 'compaction complete' -> 09:02:44.75Z failed again = SIX full-table optimize() calls in 8.6 s. Failure modes seen: 'Retryable commit conflict for version 12326/12331: This Rewrite transaction was preempted by concurrent transaction Rewrite' and 'Object at location .../_versions/18446744073709542049.manifest not found'. The retry the engine explicitly asks for is never performed. CADENCE PROOF: 6h window = 770 POST /index vs 14 compaction attempts (8 complete + 6 failed) = 55 inserts/attempt against a nominal _COMPACT_EVERY=100 — it is over-firing by ~1.8x. CAUSAL JOIN: each optimize() is a FULL-TABLE rewrite emitting a ~20 MiB fragment (5 largest data files all 19.4-20.0 MiB); firing bursts of those inside 18.1 MiB of headroom is the death event. Because the allocation is in the Rust lance extension and PID 1 unwinds, the container dies as ExitCode=0 / OOMKilled=false — so ANY triage keying on OOMKilled misses this class entirely. CORROBORATION (unplanned, disclosed by the spike): a 'docker exec python3 -c import lancedb' shares the cgroup and killed the container at 10:12:00.6Z; anon fell 726.4 -> 30.8 MiB across the restart, proving the memory is process-resident, not reclaimable page cache. done_tasks.status_note:
THREE COUPLED DEFECTS, all PO-verified at source 2026-07-25T14:50Z. Fix all three or the loop returns.

(A) POISON VALUE DEFEATS THE SORT — scripts/orch-cold-evict.sh:236. `sort_by(.created_at // "0000-00-00T00:00:00Z")` is a plain STRING sort, and the `//` alternative only substitutes when created_at is null/absent. It does NOT catch the literal string "unknown". 10 of the 16 live done[] rows carry created_at:"unknown" (ARCH-ORCH-F1, ARCH-ORCH-F2, ARCH-ORCH-QA, BCTC-CURRENT-404-INVESTIGATE, FDA-4, FDA-8, FU-LOCKSTORE-EXPIRED-GC, FU-PRESSURE-EMIT-DARK, FU-TICK-SNAPSHOT-EMIT-DARK, PM-ORCH-DASH-DECISION-DRILLDOWN). 'u' (0x75) > '2' (0x32), so after sort_by|reverse those 10 rank as the NEWEST rows, keys 0-9. They therefore consume the ENTIRE KEEP_RECENT_DONE=10 window and fail `.key >= keep_n` forever — even though they would PASS the age gate, because line 245's `try (created_at|fromdateiso8601) catch 0` maps them to epoch 0. The malformed value makes the oldest rows look newest. Schema permits it: orchStateSchema.ts:102 `created_at: z.string().optional()` — any string, no ISO-8601 refinement. No live writer of "unknown" found in scripts/ (grep clean), so this is legacy data, not an active producer.

(B) TRIGGER AND ACTION ARE ON DIFFERENT AXES — scripts/agents-flow/dev-team-tick-preflight.sh:368 fires Step 5.5 when ANY of {terminal_sprint_n>0, sprint_goal_terminal_n>0, done_n>10, dv_n>0}. Live right now: 0 / 0 / 16 / 0 — so `done_n > 10` is the SOLE live disjunct. The action it fires (orch-cold-evict.sh:242-247) evicts a done row only when `.key >= keep_n` AND created_at older than `now - DONE_MAX_AGE_DAYS*86400` (default 7d, line 66). A COUNT gate firing a COUNT-AND-AGE action cannot be self-clearing. Even with (A) fixed the loop RETURNS: the 6 well-formed done rows accumulated over 4 days (~1.5/day), so a 7-day age window holds ~10 rows on its own and done_n re-crosses 10 within roughly a week. (A) alone buys about seven days, not a fix.

(C) THE ACCEPTANCE INSTRUMENT ITSELF LIES — orch-cold-evict.sh:256 `[.task_board.done_verified // [] | .[].id // ""]`. jq's `//` fires when the LHS produces NO outputs, so on an EMPTY array this yields `[""]`, length 1. Live proof: done_verified is `[]` and signal_queue.archive is `[]`, yet --dry-run prints 'done_verified[] would evict: 1 items' and 'signal_queue.archive[] evict: 1 items'. Harmless for actual eviction (the `select(. != "")` at 258-260 drops the phantom) but it corrupts the exact report an operator or a test would read to decide whether a run did anything. Confirm with: jq -n '[[] | .[].id // ""]' -> [""]. Same shape guards n_evict_done at line 344. FIX (C) FIRST — the acceptance test for (A)/(B) reads this report.

done_tasks.title: sla-monitor's bctc threshold is NOT a policy constant — it rises 60min/hour in lockstep with the measured staleness, holding a fixed 5439-minute margin. The gate can therefore never clear and never escalates, and the 'threshold' value printed in every CRITICAL alert is meaningless.
done_tasks.status_note:
MECHANICALLY PROVEN, not inferred. PO extracted every bctc sla-monitor alert from list_unresolved_reports() over a 21-hour window (2026-07-24T17:00Z -> 2026-07-25T14:00Z, 12 samples) and differenced the two numbers in each message:
  stale=5950 thr=511 | 6010/571 | 6070/631 | 6160/721 | 6250/811 | 6340/901 | 6400/961 | 6550/1111 | 6700/1261 | 6910/1471 | 7090/1651 | 7210/1771
The set of (stale - threshold) values across all 12 samples is EXACTLY {5439}. One element. The threshold is not a duration policy — it is a second clock running 5439 minutes behind the first.

ISOLATED TO bctc, WHICH IS THE POSITIVE CONTROL THAT MAKES THIS A REAL DEFECT AND NOT A GLOBAL MISREADING: in the same alert stream over the same window, every other metric's threshold is CONSTANT — bond_maturity 10080 (7d) in all samples, signal_quality_audit 2880 (48h) in all, news 30, sbv_fx 30. Only the bctc threshold moves. So this is a bctc-specific threshold computation, not a shared formatter bug and not an artifact of how the message is rendered.

HYPOTHESIS FOR THE ROOT CAUSE, stated as a hypothesis and NOT verified at source (PO did not read the sla-monitor implementation — the next agent must): a constant difference between two quantities that both grow with wall-clock time means BOTH are ages measured from `now` against FIXED timestamps, 5439 minutes apart. That is, the code is almost certainly comparing `now - T_data` against `now - T_other` — an AGE-vs-AGE comparison — where a correct SLA compares an AGE against a DURATION. Whoever picks this up should first confirm or refute that shape before changing anything; if it is refuted, the 5439 constant still has to be explained.

OPERATIONAL COST: the bctc breach re-fires roughly hourly and has done so continuously for at least 21 hours (almost certainly far longer — 3 samples/hour of bond_maturity + signal_quality_audit + bctc dominate the 100-row unresolved-report backlog). Because the margin is fixed, the alert carries zero information about whether the situation is improving or worsening: it will print CRITICAL with a larger pair of numbers forever.

THE DEFECT. `blocks` reads as a sequencing constraint and binds NOTHING. It is write-only across the entire repo. An author who writes `blocks: ["X"]` on row A, intending "X must not start before A", has created zero enforcement — and, critically, has no way to tell the difference from a working gate by inspecting the board.

VERIFIED AT SOURCE, NOT RELAYED:
  - scripts/lib/devteam-eligibility.jq:133-141 — `effective_depends_on` unions ONLY the candidate row's own `.depends_on`, `.depends` and `.blocked_by`; inline first, then backlog-detail.json for detail_ref'd rows. It never traverses a reverse edge from any other row.
  - :161-164 — `deps_satisfied` short-circuits `true` when the effective list is empty.
  - Full grep across scripts/lib/*.jq, scripts/devteam-*.jq, scripts/orch-*.mjs, scripts/orch-*.sh, scripts/agents-flow/*.sh: NO consumer of `blocks`. The only textual matches are unrelated test-assertion prose ("... blocks idle").

LIVE POPULATION — 7 rows carry the field, and the three states are instructive:
  - INERT-BUT-INTENDED (1): FIX-BCTC-INGEST-PERIOD-IDENTITY-UNVALIDATED-VS-CONTENT -> FU-BACKFILL-REAL-FILENAMES. This was PO's own guard, written 16:49Z today, believed binding, and it was not. Now repaired by writing the reciprocal `depends_on` inline on the target. THIS IS THE PROOF THE FIELD IS A TRAP: a caller whose entire job is board correctness used it wrongly on the same day, because nothing about it signals that it does not work.
  - ACCIDENTALLY-BINDING (1): RAG-FTS-BUILD-MEMORY-BOUND -> ALPHA-S2-RAG-FTS-REBUILD-CRON. This one DOES hold — but not because of the `blocks` edge. The target independently carries `blocked_by: ["ALPHA-S2-RAG-FTS-CRON-SAFETY-GATE", "RAG-FTS-BUILD-MEMORY-BOUND"]` and status BLOCKED. Positive control for the correct shape, and evidence that the correct shape is already known and used elsewhere in the same board. Verified at source rather than assumed.
  - MALFORMED (1): FIX-MCP-SUITE-HEALTH-BASELINE's `blocks` value is not a task id or a list of them — it is a prose paragraph beginning "PUSH-AUTONOMY-1. This standing red makes any literal '0 fail on the FULL suite' reading of the push gate permanently unsatisfiable...". A separate data-quality defect that only survives because nothing ever parses the field. It is IN SCOPE for this row: whichever remedy is chosen must not silently swallow a non-list value.
  - EMPTY / harmless (4): TASK_2006, TASK_2005, ALPHA-S2-SUB5-WATCHDOG-STRETCH, ALPHA-S2-FF-SUB6-BUCKETING-HELPER all carry `blocks: []`.

REMEDY — THREE HONEST OPTIONS, po did NOT choose:
  [a] MAKE THE GATE READ THE REVERSE EDGE — extend `effective_depends_on` to also scan every lane for rows whose `blocks` contains the candidate's id. Most faithful to author intent, and fixes all existing writers retroactively. Costs a full-board scan per candidate inside a hot eligibility predicate; measure before adopting.
  [b] MAKE `blocks` AN ALIAS — have scripts/orch-apply.sh mirror `A.blocks: [X]` into `X.blocked_by += [A]` at write time, so the reverse edge is normalised into the forward field the gates already read. Keeps the eligibility predicate untouched and cheap. Needs care: mirroring must be idempotent, must not fight a hand-written `blocked_by`, and must fail loud on a non-list value (see the malformed row above) rather than mirroring garbage.
  [c] DELETE THE FIELD — strip `blocks` from all 7 rows and forbid it, forcing every sequencing intent through `depends_on`/`blocked_by`. Smallest surface, but discards genuinely useful documentation-of-intent and does nothing to stop the next author reaching for an intuitive name.
WHAT IS NOT ACCEPTABLE is leaving a field that reads as a constraint in every board dump while binding nothing. If [c] is chosen, the deletion must be paired with something that makes the mistake loud — see acceptance 3.

SCOPE ITEM DISCOVERED WHILE REPAIRING THE INSTANCE — A SECOND WAY DEP GATES CAN SILENTLY OPEN. scripts/orch-backlog-stub.sh defaults `STUB_FIELDS="id,title,priority,size,type,zone,status,sprint,detail_ref"`. `depends_on`, `depends` and `blocked_by` are NOT in the keep-set, so a re-run strips inline deps out of hot rows. Net effect: a dependency that was set correctly, later silently unset by an unrelated maintenance migration. This belongs here because it is the same failure mode by a different route: a gate that is present in the author's mental model and absent from the machine's.

signal_rows.mechanism_hypothesis: This is distinct from the already-tracked feedback_preclaim_ttl_600s_expires_under_long_agent_runs.md mechanism (TTL expiring mid-run) and from feedback_pipeline_resume_stale_placeholder_duplicate_spawn_risk.md (PO's own triage_key). Here the board row already showed claimed_at/claimed_by IN_PROGRESS stamps (written by router at 18:36:54Z, BEFORE agent-father was even spawned) yet a peer session still dispatched its own agent-father onto the identical task_id shortly after — meaning either (a) the peer's dispatch path does not board-status-check a manually-router-claimed task before spawning, checking only its own PRE-CLAIM intent-key lock (which is scoped per-agent+intent, not per-task_id, so two peers each doing 'router manual dispatch' under different intent-keys would never collide on the lock itself), or (b) an extremely narrow TOCTOU window between the write and the peer's read. (a) is the more actionable hypothesis: PRE-CLAIM's task_id namespace is 'intent:<agent>:<intent-key>', which does not encode the specific task_id being dispatched, so it cannot prevent two different router sessions from both manually-dispatching the SAME underlying task_id under two DIFFERENT intent-keys (e.g. one from a PO-BATCH pass, one from a peer's own independent BOUNDED-1/triage pass) — only same-intent-key collisions are caught. Worth a root-cause check: should manual dev-team dispatch also claim a task-level lock keyed literally to the task_id (task:<task_id>), not just the intent-key, before spawning? Self-resolved with zero harm this occurrence (complementary work, no duplicate final state) but is architecturally reproducible any time two peer sessions independently decide to manually-dispatch the same backlog/ready row within the same short window.

decision_journal.decision: RECURRING-BUG-ESCALATION (4th touch of the single-digit-RSI / gia-0 class). Did NOT re-open FIX-ALERT-ENGINE-RSI-SINGLEDIGIT (kept in review[], gate stays RED — it is a downstream consumer in the WRONG zone apps/alert-engine). Did NOT re-open the closed OHLCV-seeder P0s (their fix was real + done_verified but NON-GENERIC: migrated aggregator/backfill/pushPrices through writeOhlcvBatch, MISSED the foreign-flow writer). MINTED 2 coupled NEW tasks: (1) ARCH-OHLCV-WRITER-SSOT-DURABLE to architect (durable producer root: route the last bypassing daily_ohlcv writer, writeForeignFlowToOhlcv, through the writeOhlcvBatch SSOT so its all-zero stub becomes an honest-gap NULL-OHLCV row, never a fake 0 latest-candle; close the whole writer-bypass class), and (2) FIX-ALERT-SCAN-REJECT-STUB-BAR-P0 to dev-mcp-server (consumer defense-in-depth: taAlertScanJob + bbAlertScanJob reject a latest bar with close<=0 OR volume<=0 before computing RSI/BB — guards the VALUE not just the candle count). Routed 2 drained signals.
decision_journal.root-cause: writeForeignFlowToOhlcv (apps/mcp-server/src/infrastructure/db/ohlcvForeignFlowStore.ts L58-69) BYPASSES writeOhlcvBatch and INSERTs a stub row open/high/low/close=0,volume=0 ON CONFLICT(code,date) when the foreign-flow fetch (gated to VN market open 02:00Z) arrives BEFORE the real OHLCV bar. taAlertScanJob/bbAlertScanJob CANDLE_SQL (SELECT close FROM daily_ohlcv WHERE date>=-60d ORDER BY day ASC) read that C=0 stub as TODAY latest candle: Wilder RSI with a final 0 after a ~27000 real close collapses to single-digit across ALL tickers simultaneously (CTG 3.4 / SSI 6.8 / VCB 3.7 on a +0.48% day = statistically impossible), and close=Math.round(0)=0 yields gia 0 duoi BB spam (msg 783-790, 02:15-03:15Z). Later the real OHLCV bar UPSERTs over the stub so canonical reads clean by 04:30Z. This is feedback_ohlcv_startup_purge_defeated_by_backfill_seeder: a re-seeding WRITER defeats the repair; fix the WRITER not the residue; trace ALL writers into daily_ohlcv (this was the un-migrated straggler).
decision_journal.what-considered: (1) re-open the closed OHLCV-seeder P0 — REJECTED: those fixes were real + done_verified; the bug is a DIFFERENT writer (foreign-flow store) they never covered; re-opening would hide that it is a coverage gap not a regression. (2) straight FIX to dev-alert-engine — REJECTED: 4th recurrence, owner zone proven WRONG twice (real root is a WRITER in apps/mcp-server, not alert-engine); recurring-bug-escalation mandates architect for the durable writer-SSOT root. (3) only patch the consumer scan guard — REJECTED as the SOLE fix: it stops the spam but leaves a fake C=0 OHLCV bar in the served table (poisons get_price_history / every other reader); the producer must stop writing fake 0-bars too (/goal#1 no-fake-data: illiquid means honest gap, never a 0 seed). (4) architect durable producer root (writer-SSOT across ALL bypass writers) PLUS dev consumer defense-in-depth guard, BOTH P0 — CHOSEN: kill the fake bar at the writer AND fail-closed at the reader.
decision_journal.why-change: Router LIVE-RAW-verified the symptom (msg 783-790) and the canonical-clean-by-04:30Z repair window; PO code-traced the SPECIFIC writer (writeForeignFlowToOhlcv C=0 stub) the migrated-writer set missed, and confirmed neither scan job rejects a C=0 / zero-volume latest bar. No change from router hypothesis — confirmed at code level and named the exact writer.
